title: Ce qui sera déjà terminé
summary: Express completion before a future point and recognize future-perfect conjectures about the past.
objectives: Form the future perfect across regular, irregular, modal and être verbs.
Distinguish future completion from conjectural past explanations.
Use French future forms after quand and dès que.

sections.title: Future auxiliary plus participle
paragraphs: The future perfect (futur antérieur) views an action as complete before a future reference point. Use future avoir or être plus a past participle. Avoir forms: j'aurai terminé, tu auras terminé, il/elle/on aura terminé, nous aurons terminé, vous aurez terminé, ils/elles auront terminé.

Regular participles include parlé, choisi/fini, vendu/attendu. Irregular participles include eu (avoir), été (être), fait, pris, compris, vu, lu, reçu. Combine any of these with all six auxiliary forms: j'aurai eu, tu auras eu, il/elle/on aura eu, nous aurons eu, vous aurez eu, ils/elles auront eu; replace eu with été, fait or another relevant participle.
The future aurai differs from conditional aurais in spelling and, for some speakers, pronunciation. Use the future when stating future completion, not an imagined conditional result.
points: Agreement rules do not change: a preceding direct object can make an avoir participle agree.

examples.french: D'ici jeudi, nous **aurons préparé** la salle.
examples.english: By Thursday, we will have prepared the room.
examples.note: The deadline is a future reference point.

examples.french: À midi, vous **aurez fini** la première partie.
examples.english: At noon, you will have finished the first part.
examples.note: A completed stage, not an action still in progress.

examples.french: Quand ils **auront vendu** la maison, ils déménageront.
examples.english: When they have sold the house, they will move.
examples.note: English uses present perfect after when; French uses future perfect.

examples.french: En décembre, elle **aura été** responsable pendant un an.
examples.english: In December, she will have been in charge for a year.

examples.french: Après cet atelier, vous **aurez fait** votre premier montage.
examples.english: After this workshop, you will have made your first edit.

mistakes.avoid: Demain soir, j'aurais terminé, c'est certain.
mistakes.prefer: Demain soir, j'aurai terminé, c'est certain.
mistakes.why: The intended assured future completion uses aurai, not conditional aurais.

sections.title: Arrival and reflexive completion
paragraphs: Être forms: je serai arrivé(e), tu seras arrivé(e), il sera arrivé/elle sera arrivée/on sera arrivé(e)(s), nous serons arrivé(e)s, vous serez arrivé(e)(s), ils seront arrivés/elles seront arrivées. Replace arrivé by the participle of another être verb, such as parti, revenu, né or devenu, and agree with the subject.

Reflexive pronouns remain before the auxiliary: je me serai inscrit(e), tu te seras inscrit(e), il/elle/on se sera inscrit(e)(s), nous nous serons inscrit(e)s, vous vous serez inscrit(e)(s), ils/elles se seront inscrit(e)s. Check the pronoun's object role for agreement with other reflexive verbs.

examples.french: À ton arrivée, les ouvrières **seront parties**.
examples.english: By the time you arrive, the female workers will have left.

examples.french: Dès que nous **nous serons inscrits**, nous recevrons le programme.
examples.english: As soon as we have registered, we will receive the programme.
examples.note: Masculine/mixed nous; a later action follows completion.

examples.french: Les valises qu'elle **aura sorties** attendront dans l'entrée.
examples.english: The suitcases she has taken out will be waiting in the entrance.
examples.note: Transitive sortir uses avoir; que triggers feminine plural agreement.

sections.title: Completion and plausible explanations are different readings
paragraphs: Vouloir, pouvoir and devoir use voulu, pu and dû. The complete auxiliary series is aurai, auras, aura, aurons, aurez, auront: j'aurai voulu/pu/dû, tu auras voulu/pu/dû, il/elle/on aura voulu/pu/dû, nous aurons voulu/pu/dû, vous aurez voulu/pu/dû, ils/elles auront voulu/pu/dû. Add an infinitive for the intended or necessary action.

In future completion, aura pu can describe an opportunity realized by a later point; aura dû can summarize a necessity before then. In a conjecture, future perfect can suggest what probably happened already: il aura oublié = he must have forgotten/probably forgot. Aura voulu suggests an inferred intention, aura pu an inferred possibility, aura dû an inferred necessity. Context, not the form alone, separates these readings.
points: A conjectural future perfect is not the same as conditional-past advice: tu auras dû partir can infer you had to leave; tu aurais dû partir means you should have left.

examples.french: À la fin du stage, chacun **aura pu** essayer les deux machines.
examples.english: By the end of the placement, everyone will have had the opportunity to try both machines.

examples.french: Avant de rendre son mémoire, elle **aura dû** vérifier chaque référence.
examples.english: Before submitting her dissertation, she will have had to check every reference.
examples.note: Necessity completed before a future limit.

examples.french: Il n'a rien dit : il **aura voulu** nous éviter un souci.
examples.english: He said nothing: he probably wanted to spare us a worry.
examples.note: An inference about a past intention.

examples.french: Elle ne répond pas ; elle **aura dû** partir plus tôt.
examples.english: She is not answering; she probably had to leave earlier.
examples.note: Conjecture about past necessity, not advice.

practice.prompt: Supply choisir in the future perfect: D'ici lundi, nous ___ le lieu.
Supply prendre in the future perfect: À ce moment-là, elle ___ sa décision.
Supply revenir in the future perfect: À vingt heures, mes filles ___ .
Supply pouvoir in the future perfect: À la fin du cours, vous ___ pratiquer chaque forme.
practice.explanation: A completed opportunity by a future endpoint.

practice.prompt: Supply vendre in the future perfect: Quand tu ___ le vélo, appelle-moi.
practice.explanation: French uses future perfect after quand for future completion.

practice.prompt: Supply avoir in the future perfect: Demain, j'___ trois entretiens cette semaine.
Supply être in the future perfect: En juin, nous ___ voisins pendant dix ans.
Supply partir in the future perfect: À huit heures, le dernier train ___ .
Supply vouloir in the future perfect for a past inference: Il a refusé le cadeau ; il ___ rester indépendant.
practice.explanation: The context infers a past intention.

practice.prompt: Supply devoir in the future perfect: Avant l'ouverture, ils ___ déplacer tous les meubles.
practice.explanation: Future-perfect necessity; dû keeps its accent.

practice.prompt: Supply se préparer in the future perfect, for feminine plural elles: À neuf heures, elles ___ .
practice.explanation: Reflexive pronoun before être, with agreement.

practice.prompt: In Il est absent ; il aura oublié la réunion, what is the future perfect doing?
practice.explanation: This is conjecture, not aurait dû advice.

practice.prompt: Supply terminer in the future perfect: À la fermeture, nous ___ l'inventaire.
practice.explanation: Future avoir plus regular -er participle for completion before a future point.

practice.prompt: Supply faire in the future perfect: Vous ___ le plus difficile avant midi.
Supply lire in the future perfect: Dès qu'elle ___ le contrat, elle répondra.
Supply pouvoir in the future perfect: D'ici ce soir, nous ___ parler à chacun.
practice.explanation: Future completion of the opportunity to speak.

practice.prompt: Supply arriver in the future perfect: À cette heure-là, la directrice ___ .

production_task.prompt: Give a realistic schedule for moving an association into a new office. State three things that will be complete by different future points, using both auxiliaries and one modal.
production_task.model_answer: Vendredi soir, nous aurons emballé les archives. Samedi à midi, les premiers bénévoles seront arrivés. Avant l'ouverture lundi, chacun aura pu visiter les nouveaux locaux.
production_task.translation: On Friday evening, we will have packed the archives. By noon on Saturday, the first volunteers will have arrived. Before opening on Monday, everyone will have had the opportunity to visit the new premises.
rubric: Each future-perfect form has an explicit reference point.
Future rather than conditional auxiliaries are used.
Arrival uses être and appropriate agreement.
The modal describes a coherent completed opportunity.
